topic: Calendar-exhaustion covariance frontier for staggered-DiD calendar effects. In the exact known-covariance Gaussian not-yet-treated score experiment generated by fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections, characterize global minimax MSE and shortest uniformly honest expected length for a Holder-smooth late-calendar ATT while bounded cohort deviations remain unrestricted. Work uniformly over growing T, N/T>=1, and 1<=m<=delta T. Derive the nested covariance, phase diagram, attaining estimator and interval/band, matched lower bounds, and exact fixed-marginal diagonal-order comparison. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: sparse coefficient algebra yields an exhaustion component and nested common floor, verified numerically for T=3,...,8. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: uniform bounded lifts with matched information. EARLY KILL TEST: dimension-free lift and Mahalanobis-energy bounds for canonical boundary bumps.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the global minimax MSE for a Holder-smooth late-calendar ATT in the exact known-covariance Gaussian score experiment induced by staggered-adoption repeated cross sections when cohort-specific deviations are only uniformly bounded?

source_refs.claim: Defines group-time ATTs for panel and repeated-cross-section DiD, including calendar-time aggregations and inference.
source_refs.author: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

source_refs.claim: Derives robust efficient estimators for prespecified weighted event-study effects under unrestricted heterogeneity and discusses long-run effects and growing T.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Xavier Jaravel, and Jann Spiess

source_refs.claim: Characterizes minimax estimation of linear functionals in Gaussian inverse experiments through a modulus of continuity.
source_refs.author: David L. Donoho

open_problems.why_unsolved: Callaway-Sant'Anna identify and estimate calendar-time aggregates, while Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess obtain efficiency for fixed weighted effects and only limited growing-T asymptotics; neither optimizes worst-case risk over a Holder calendar path coupled to bounded, otherwise unrestricted cohort deviations. Donoho's modulus machinery applies only after the triangular score operator and its nested covariance are reduced to a tractable parameter-space modulus. The presolve exhaustion-component and common-floor algebra remains a hypothesis requiring uniform verification beyond T=3,...,8. Even if that decomposition holds, a least-favorable boundary bump must be lifted through the cohort-time nuisance surface without a T-dependent violation of the cohort bound or loss of Mahalanobis information.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-sample or uniform-asymptotic formula for minimax squared-error risk over all N/T>=1 and 1<=m<=delta T, with a proved nested-covariance decomposition, explicit phase diagram, attaining estimator, and matched modulus or two-point lower bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction moves from the empirical importance of event studies to heterogeneous-effect failures and then to a target-specific efficiency problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Event studies are ubiquitous -> heterogeneous effects invalidate conventional long-run coefficients -> robust analysis requires explicit targets and comparison sets -> calendar exhaustion calls for a minimax frontier for the late-calendar target

method_exemplars.technique: Compute the modulus of continuity of a linear functional in a Gaussian inverse experiment and use its least-favorable pair to derive an affine estimator and matched risk lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The late-calendar ATT is a linear functional observed through a nonidentity score operator, so its risk is governed by signal separation relative to covariance-weighted information.

method_exemplars.technique: Solve a Holder boundary optimal-recovery problem using optimized local-polynomial weights and translate worst-case bias and variance into minimax MSE.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Calendar exhaustion makes the late ATT a boundary functional, with nested DiD covariance and cohort-nuisance lifting replacing ordinary independent regression noise.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function and its covariance before constructing an efficient ATT estimator and limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest published score-level account of how repeated cross sections alter DiD information, which is the covariance input to the proposed Gaussian experiment.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the shortest uniformly honest expected length for confidence intervals for the late-calendar ATT, and where does its phase diagram differ from the global minimax-MSE frontier?

source_refs.claim: Constructs uniformly honest DiD and event-study inference under bounded trend violations and proves near-optimal expected length for important restriction classes.
source_refs.author: Ashesh Rambachan and Jonathan Roth

source_refs.claim: Derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and expected-length efficiency bounds for linear functionals over convex regression classes with known Gaussian variance.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: Provides valid inference for robust event-study estimators but does not optimize honest length under calendar smoothness and terminal control exhaustion.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Xavier Jaravel, and Jann Spiess

open_problems.why_unsolved: Rambachan-Roth optimize robustness to parallel-trend departures in a reduced event-study coefficient model, whereas Armstrong-Kolesar optimize Gaussian intervals after the observation operator and convex class are specified. Neither class combines a Holder restriction on a calendar component, an unrestricted-but-bounded cohort component, and a nested covariance whose common floor changes as not-yet-treated cohorts disappear. Standard bias-aware intervals therefore do not determine whether exhaustion changes only constants or creates distinct variance-, smoothness-, and nuisance-limited regimes; the relevant ordered modulus also depends on the still-unresolved bounded lift.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp minimax maximum-expected-length characterization among all uniformly 1-alpha honest intervals, with an explicit bias-aware interval attaining it and matching ordered-modulus or testing lower bounds uniformly in T, N, and m.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames honest DiD inference as the operational consequence of weakening a conventional identifying restriction and makes interval length a first-class performance criterion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact DiD assumptions are fragile -> bounded deviations produce extrapolation uncertainty -> honest inference must account for worst-case bias -> late-calendar exhaustion requires the shortest honest interval under smoothness plus cohort nuisance

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordered moduli between convex parameter sets to construct finite-sample Gaussian confidence intervals and prove sharp expected-length efficiency bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is an honest expected-length problem for a linear causal functional, with the new work residing in computing the modulus under the DiD score operator and nested covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate achievable expected length to between-class ordered moduli and construct intervals attaining the resulting adaptation bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower-bound geometry can distinguish genuinely different exhaustion-information regimes from ordinary bandwidth choices.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct bias-aware honest intervals for Holder boundary functionals and compare MSE-optimal with interval-optimal tuning.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest benchmark for comparing MSE and honest-length frontiers at a boundary before introducing calendar-exhaustion covariance.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax-width uniformly honest simultaneous band for the final m calendar-time ATTs when m may grow up to delta T under Holder smoothness and bounded unrestricted cohort deviations?

source_refs.claim: Develops multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous confidence bands for collections of group-time ATTs and their aggregates in staggered DiD, including repeated cross sections.
source_refs.author: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

source_refs.claim: Constructs doubly robust uniform confidence bands for group-time conditional ATTs using empirical-process approximation and multiplier bootstrap.
source_refs.author: Shunsuke Imai, Lei Qin, and Takahide Yanagi

source_refs.claim: Proves lower bounds for confidence-band width and near-attaining finite-sample procedures while showing unrestricted adaptation is impossible.
source_refs.author: Christopher R. Genovese and Larry Wasserman

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing staggered-DiD bands control simultaneous sampling error for identified group-time effects; they do not optimize width when the terminal calendar path is learned by smooth extrapolation as the control pool is exhausted. Classical band theory observes the curve directly or through standard regression noise and lacks a shrinking triangular not-yet-treated design, a nested common covariance floor, and bounded high-dimensional cohort nuisance. As m grows, the Gaussian maximum, smoothness bias, and exhaustion floor can dominate in different regimes, so pointwise-optimal weights with a generic sup-t critical value need not be minimax.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit simultaneous 1-alpha band for the last m calendar ATTs with a sharp uniform formula for minimax maximum or average expected width, a phase diagram in N, T, m, and smoothness, and matched multi-hypothesis or Gaussian-width lower bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates simultaneous reporting of heterogeneous group-time and aggregated ATT paths and separates estimands, estimators, and uniform inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered timing creates many group-time causal effects -> aggregation reveals calendar and dynamic heterogeneity -> simultaneous bands are needed for an effect path -> the terminal path requires minimax bands accounting for calendar exhaustion

method_exemplars.technique: Derive confidence-band width lower bounds through packing and testing arguments and construct a near-attaining Gaussian band.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is a growing vector of boundary values, so band optimality requires controlling simultaneous distinguishability across terminal bumps.

method_exemplars.technique: Linearize staggered-DiD effect functions and use Gaussian empirical-process approximation plus multiplier bootstrap for uniform coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest DiD-specific band construction, to be adapted using exact nested score covariance and explicit worst-case smoothness bias.

method_exemplars.technique: Use multiscale estimators and self-similarity to characterize when honest adaptive Holder bands exist and attain optimal width.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its necessity arguments identify the extra restrictions needed if the calendar band must adapt to unknown smoothness.

open_problems.open_problem: At fixed coordinate variances, when does nested calendar-exhaustion covariance yield smaller or larger minimax risk and honest interval length than its diagonal-covariance counterpart for a late-calendar ATT?

source_refs.claim: Shows that panel and repeated-cross-section DiD information and efficiency can differ at first order because their score covariance structures differ.
source_refs.author: Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna and Jun B. Zhao

source_refs.claim: Characterizes efficient robust event-study weighting and allows known heteroskedasticity and dependence, making covariance geometry central to efficiency.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Xavier Jaravel, and Jann Spiess

source_refs.claim: Uses Loewner covariance dominance and Anderson's theorem to obtain stochastic ordering of Gaussian procedures for symmetric convex acceptance regions.
source_refs.author: Peter L. Cohen and Colin B. Fogarty
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: The usual Loewner comparison cannot order two distinct covariance matrices with identical diagonals because a positive-semidefinite difference with zero diagonal must vanish. Nested calendar covariance may reduce noise for smooth contrasts while making cohort-nuisance directions harder to separate. Existing DiD efficiency calculations do not give an exact fixed-marginal ordering over a Holder-plus-bounded-nuisance class, and Gaussian comparison results for symmetric convex acceptance regions do not directly compare minimax functional risk or expected interval length in this non-Loewner-ordered setting.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact necessary-and-sufficient or closed-form regime comparison of the covariance-weighted modulus, minimax MSE, and shortest honest expected length under nested versus diagonal covariance with identical marginals, including equality and reversal regions.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats covariance and efficiency differences across DiD data structures as economically meaningful rather than as routine variance correction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Panel and repeated-cross-section DiD share an ATT target -> their information differs through covariance -> efficiency losses can be first order -> fixed marginals isolate the unresolved contribution of calendar-exhaustion dependence

method_exemplars.technique: Translate Loewner covariance dominance into stochastic dominance using Anderson's theorem and isolate exactly where symmetry and covariance ordering enter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a nearby causal-inference covariance-comparison proof and exposes why equal-diagonal nested and diagonal experiments require a parameter-class-specific argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare Gaussian experiments by computing the covariance-weighted modulus of the target functional rather than seeking a global matrix order.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The two covariances can be compared through their Mahalanobis geometries on the same Holder-plus-nuisance difference set, directly matching the desired risk and interval ordering.

open_problems.open_problem: Can canonical Holder boundary bumps for a late-calendar ATT be lifted into bounded cohort-time treatment-effect surfaces with dimension-free sup-norm control while preserving their calendar signal and Mahalanobis energy under the not-yet-treated nested covariance?

source_refs.claim: Obtains minimax lower bounds from least-favorable alternatives whose functional separation is large relative to Gaussian information distance.
source_refs.author: David L. Donoho

source_refs.claim: Computes Holder boundary minimaxity using optimal-recovery extremal functions in nonparametric regression.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: Allows unrestricted cohort and time heterogeneity in robust event-study estimation and highlights the difficulty of long-run effects when valid comparisons disappear.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Xavier Jaravel, and Jann Spiess

source_refs.excerpt: There is a finite B, independent of Q,T,|X|,|H|, for the actual observed experiments.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Optimal-recovery proofs place an extremal bump directly in the observed regression mean, whereas the late-calendar parameter is an aggregate of a cohort-time surface. The first proof step therefore becomes a constrained right-inverse problem: lift the calendar bump into cohort cells while maintaining a dimension-free cohort-deviation bound. A naive lift may accumulate as the not-yet-treated set shrinks, while a bounded lift may disperse the bump and destroy the covariance-weighted information match. The prior POMDP proposal supplies a structurally analogous but still to-prove dimension-free observed-information step; its Markov-membership and filtering arguments do not establish the required DiD lift. Thus the numerically observed low-T exhaustion algebra cannot yet support uniform matched lower bounds.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform dimension-free lifting lemma mapping every canonical terminal Holder bump to an admissible repeated-cross-section DiD submodel, with explicit two-sided comparison between full-data divergence and score-experiment Mahalanobis energy, or a counterexample specifying the T, m, and cohort-share regime where such a lift is impossible.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames unrestricted cohort heterogeneity and the disappearance of valid long-run comparisons as structural features of event-study analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Robust event studies retain cohort-time heterogeneity -> long-run valid comparisons become scarce -> smooth calendar structure offers controlled extrapolation -> matched minimax bounds require a feasible dimension-free lift of boundary alternatives

method_exemplars.technique: Construct the least-favorable Holder boundary function through optimal recovery and balance its functional separation against sampling variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its extremal boundary bump is the donor construction whose separation must survive lifting into the staggered-DiD cohort surface.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert a feasible least-favorable pair with controlled Gaussian information distance into matched minimax estimation and confidence lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once a bounded lift with matched Mahalanobis energy is established, its modulus argument supplies the lower-bound side of the desired frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the truncated-history two-point Le Cam architecture and observed-filtration information contraction, replacing latent-depth survival with calendar-boundary bump energy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require a high-dimensional model-class perturbation whose observable information stays dimension-free while target separation remains at the minimax scale.

literature_map:
Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, ReStud) derive robust efficient event-study estimation, flag spurious long-run identification, and allow only controlled growth of T.
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics) make ATT(g,t) primitive, cover repeated cross sections, define calendar-time aggregation, and provide simultaneous bootstrap bands.
Sun and Abraham (2021, Journal of Econometrics) show dynamic TWFE coefficients are contaminated by heterogeneous cohort effects.
de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2020, AER) and Goodman-Bacon (2021, Journal of Econometrics) establish heterogeneous-effect weighting failures behind modern staggered DiD.
Wing, Freedman, and Hollingsworth (2024, NBER w32054) separate calendar time from event time and trim group-time effects to prevent changing-composition artifacts.
Schmidheiny and Siegloch (2023, Journal of Applied Econometrics) show endpoint binning identifies long-run dynamics only by imposing substantive constant-effect restrictions.
Roth (2024, arXiv:2401.12309) studies how recent DiD estimators map into event-study plots and emphasizes changing cohort composition across event times.
Roth, Sant'Anna, Bilinski, and Poe (2023, Journal of Econometrics) synthesize staggered timing, parallel-trend sensitivity, and inference frameworks without providing a calendar-exhaustion minimax theory.
Rambachan and Roth (2023, ReStud) give honest DiD inference under bounded trend violations and near-optimal fixed-length intervals, supplying the closest causal robustness template.
Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020, Journal of Econometrics) derive repeated-cross-section DiD efficiency bounds and show covariance-induced information losses can be first order.
Athey and Imbens (2022, Journal of Econometrics) give exact design-based staggered-adoption results for panel data, a distinct covariance setting from the repeated-cross-section Gaussian frontier.
Donoho (1994), Armstrong and Kolesar (2018), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2020) supply Gaussian-modulus, honest-interval, and Holder-boundary optimal-recovery machinery.
Cai and Low (2004), Genovese and Wasserman (2008), and Bull (2012) clarify expected-length and band-width lower bounds and the limits of smoothness adaptation.
Imai, Qin, and Yanagi (2023, arXiv:2305.02185) provide a staggered-DiD uniform-band construction for identified conditional effects rather than terminal smooth extrapolation.
The scan found no paper combining late-calendar ATT extrapolation, exact nested not-yet-treated covariance, bounded unrestricted cohort deviations, growing T and m, and matched minimax MSE and honest-length lower bounds.
